IS t 11239( Part 4 ) - 1985

Indian Standard
METHODS OF TEST FOR RIGID CELLULAR THERMAL INSULATION MATERIALS
PART 4 WATER VAPOUR TRANSMISSION RATE

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 12 March 1985, after the draft finalized by the Thermal Insulation Materials Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council.
0.2 In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been drawn from ISO/R 1663-1970 ` Plastics - Determination of water vapour transmission rate of rigid cellular plastics `, issued by the International Organization for Standardization. 0.3 In reporting the result of a test made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2 - 1960*.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the method for determination of water vapour transmisssion rate, water vapour permeance and water vapour permeability of rigid cellular thermal insulation materials. Rigid cellular materials with thicknesses from 3 to 80 mm and which may, as integral contain natural skins or adhered facings of some part of the material, different material, may be tested by this method.
2. TERMINOLOGY

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, 19657 and the following shall apply.

the definitions

given

in IS : 3069rate unit and

2.1.1 Water Vapour Transmission Rate - Water vapour transmission is the quantity of water vapour transmitted per unit time through area of material under specified conditions of temperature, humidity thickness.
fGlossary

*liules for rounding off numerical values ( rcoiscd ). of terms, symbols and units relating to thermal insulation materials. 3

IS : 11239 ( Part 4 ) - 1985 2.1.2 IV&r I-uJ~,our Pcrmeance - Water vapour permeance is the quotient rate divided by the vapour pressure of the water vapour transmission difference between the two faces of the specimen during the test.
2.1.3 Water Vapour Petmeability - Water vapour permeability is the quantity of water vapour transmitted per unit time through a given area of the material per unit of vapour pressure difference between its two faces for unit thickness. 3. PRINCIPLE

is hermatically sealed to the open mouth of a test dish containing a desiccant. The assembly is then placed in a temperature and humidity controlled atmosphere. Periodic weighings cf the assembly are made to determine the rate of water vapour transmission through the specimen into the desiccant. 3.2 The test is carried conditions: a) 38 fout at the following temperature and humidity 2 percent. 2 2

6.1 Each test specimen shall be in the form of a cylinder, with a diameter cut to fit exactly ( push fit ) the beaker or dish. The thickness of the test specimen shall not be less than 3 mm nor greater than 80 mm. The minimum exposure area shall be 32 cm2. A groove may be cut in the edge of the test specimen to farihtate the escape of air when mounting in the beaker or dish. The specimens may, as an integral part of the material, contain natural skins or adhered facings of some different material. 6.2 A minimum of five specimens shall be tested. 5

IS : 11239 ( Part

4) - 1985

6.3 When the material

to be tested is suspected of being anisotropic, the test specimens shall be cut such that the parallel faces are normal to the direction of vapour flow of the product in its intended use.

6.4 When the materials are faced with natural skins or adhered facings which are different for the two sides, the test specimens shall be tested with the vapour Auw in the same direction as in the intended use. If the correction of intended use relative to the facings is not known, a duplicate set of specimens shall be prepared so that test can be made and reported for each direction of vapour flow. 7. PROCEDURE

7.1 Measure

the thickness of the test specimens at each quadrant to the nearest 0.1 mm, in accordance with IS : 11239 ( Part 1 )-1985* and average the results. 7.2 Place a layer of anhydrous calcium chloride, of approximately 20 mm depth, in the bottom of each beaker or dish as shown in Fig. 1. It may be desirable to place a support made of dry material such as closed cell cellular plastic in the bottom of the dish or beaker in order to bring the desiccant closer to the test specimen. 7.3 Insert the test specimen into a beaker or dish. Place the metal template centrally on the top surface and apply the melted sealant along its circumference in order to give a complete seal between the test specimen and the wall of the beaker or dish and provide a well defined exposed area on top of the specimen. #`After the sealant has set, carefully remove the template. 7.4 Weigh each of the five beakers or dishes with test in position to the nearest 1 mg. Place the beakers or constant temperature or constant humidity chamber required test-conditions or in the desiccator containing solution and placed in a constant temperature chamber required test temperature. specimens mounted dishes either in a maintained at the the recommended maintained at the

7.5 At intervals of approximately 24 hours, quickly remove the beakers or dishes from the chamber or room or the desiccator and store them in the transfer desiccator at room temperature for 30 f 1 min: then weigh each specimen mounted beaker or dish to the nearest 1 mg. After weighing, shake each beaker or dish assembly to mix the desiccant, than return the specimens to the chamber or room or the desiccator maintained at constant temperature.
NOTEIt is not necessary to place the beaker in the transfer desiccator test wibighings are conducted in the same constant temperature and humidity *Methods of test for cellular thermal insulation materials: Part 1 Dimensions. if the room.
